sections.reason: Title block, Status of this Memo, copyright notice, Abstract and table of contents. The Abstract says what the memo adds to RADIUS and binds no speaker.
Introduction. States what RADIUS and EAP are, and carries the RFC 2865 rule that a NAS must not implement the attributes for a service it cannot offer, in its EAP form.
Specification of Requirements. The RFC 2119 key-words paragraph. No obligation of its own.

Terminology. Defines authenticator, peer, authentication server, silently discard, displayable message, NAS, service and session. Two of those definitions carry obligations, sites 1.2:1 and 1.2:2; 'silently discard' carries two SHOULDs captured as RFC3579-1.2-3.
RADIUS Support for EAP. Says why the pass-through architecture exists and that a NAS may mix local authentication with pass-through, which is the MAY captured as RFC3579-2-1.

Protocol Overview. The conversation itself: who sends the first EAP-Request, how the NAS encapsulates a Response, what ends the conversation, EAP-Start, and the User-Name copying rule that lets a non-EAP-aware proxy forward the request.

Invalid Packets. The NAS header validation, the Error-Cause 202 branch, and the RADIUS server's fatal and non-fatal error handling. The DoS advice at the end is written as 'it is advisable' and 'is recommended' in lower case, and binds nobody.
Retransmission. Describes how Session-Timeout in an Access-Challenge sets the EAP retransmission timer for that one EAP-Request. Indicative prose, no obligation.
Fragmentation. One obligation, on the RADIUS server, not to exceed a Framed-MTU the NAS supplied. The NAS half is written as 'may be included'.
Alternative Uses. RADIUS-encapsulated EAP between a RADIUS server and a security server. One obligation, on the RADIUS server.
Usage Guidelines. A heading over 2.6.1 to 2.6.5 with no body text of its own.
Identifier Space. One obligation, on RADIUS server implementations, to keep the EAP Identifier spaces of distinct sessions apart.

Role Reversal. Says role reversal is not supported, with the obligation on the RADIUS server to reject an Access-Request encapsulating an EAP-Request, and a SHOULD on the same actor about the Nak it includes.
Conflicting Messages. Three NAS obligations, all captured, plus the SHOULD list of combinations a RADIUS server is told not to send.
Priority. One NAS obligation about the order in which attributes and the Accept/Reject indication are processed.

Displayable Messages. The RADIUS server's encapsulation obligation, the exclusion of Reply-Message from any EAP-bearing message, and the NAS SHOULD to discard a Reply-Message rather than translate it.
Attributes. The NAS identification attributes an Access-Request carries, and the RADIUS server's obligation to echo User-Name.
EAP-Message. The attribute format, the ordering and single-EAP-packet rules, the Message-Authenticator protection rule, and the calculate-and-discard obligations on each of the two roles.

Message-Authenticator. The attribute format and the HMAC-MD5 construction. The construction itself is written without an RFC 2119 keyword, so the site scan does not see it, and it is declared here as an unsourced id: 'MUST calculate the correct value' at sites 3.1:4 and 3.1:6 has no meaning without the formula this section states.
Table of Attributes. One obligation in the body, that neither attribute appears in an Accounting-Request. The table rows, its three notes and its legend are the section '0' the site scan derives.
The Section 3.3 Table of Attributes itself: the per-packet-type counts, Notes 1 to 3, and the legend that defines the cell values. Note 1 carries two obligations and the legend carries none.
Security Considerations. A heading over 4.1 to 4.3 with no body text of its own.

Security Requirements. The ten-item threat list and the statement that confidentiality, data origin authentication, integrity and replay protection are needed. Written in indicative prose with no keyword.

Security Protocol. The IPsec profile for RADIUS: the transforms that must be supported, the zero-length shared secret where ESP with a non-null transform carries the traffic, and the IKE mode and identity payload advice.
Security Issues. A heading and the list of the ten vulnerabilities 4.3.1 to 4.3.10 expand.
Privacy Issues. One SHOULD, to protect RADIUS with IPsec ESP, restating Section 4.2's advice.
Spoofing and Hijacking. The SHOULD to use Message-Authenticator in an Access-Request with no User-Password, captured as RFC3579-4.3.2-1, and the restatement of the Section 3.1 protection rule.
Dictionary Attacks. Quotes RFC 2865's shared-secret advice and recommends IPsec ESP. The quoted SHOULD belongs to RFC 2865.
Known Plaintext Attacks. Explains the User-Password keystream reuse problem and states one obligation, that an EAP NAS's shared secret is not reused by a NAS using User-Password.
Replay Attacks. Describes what RADIUS does and does not give for replay protection. Indicative prose, no obligation.
Negotiation Attacks. The downgrade rules: what the authenticating peer must do when EAP was expected, what the NAS must attempt, and what the RADIUS server or proxy must answer.
Impersonation. Quotes RFC 2865 Section 3 on choosing the shared secret by source address, and states SHOULDs on RADIUS proxies. Ze is neither the RADIUS server nor a proxy.
Man in the Middle Attacks. One SHOULD, that EAP methods incorporate their own per-packet integrity protection. That obligation is on the EAP method, which RFC 3748 and the method's own RFC govern.

Separation of Authenticator and Authentication Server. Explains what mutual authentication means when the two are on different hosts, and that the MSK must reach the authenticator. The key transport mechanism is stated to be out of scope for this document.
Multiple Databases. Recommends consolidating the security server's and the RADIUS server's user stores. No obligation, and the actor is the deployment.
IANA Considerations. 'This specification does not create any new registries, or define any new RADIUS attributes or values.'
References. A heading over 6.1 and 6.2.
Informative References, and the non-RFC citations IEEE802, IEEE8021X, MD5Attack, Masters and NASREQ.

sites.quote: As noted in [RFC2865], a Network Access Server (NAS) that does not implement a given service MUST NOT implement the RADIUS attributes for that service.
sites.reason: The sentence opens 'As noted in [RFC2865]' and restates RFC 2865 Section 1.1. The obligation belongs to RFC 2865, whose summary carries it as RFC2865-1.1-1.

sites.quote: This implies that a NAS that is unable to offer EAP service MUST NOT implement the RADIUS attributes for EAP.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS, the role ze plays: ze is the RADIUS client (internal/component/radius/client.go) and the device the operator logs in to. This document's own EAP-specific statement of the RFC 2865 rule quoted in the preceding sentence. Captured as RFC3579-1-1 at [MUST NOT].

sites.quote: A NAS MUST treat a RADIUS Access-Accept requesting an unavailable service as an Access-Reject instead.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS, the role ze plays: ze is the RADIUS client (internal/component/radius/client.go) and the device the operator logs in to. Captured as RFC3579-1-2 at [MUST]. Ze already rejects an Access-Accept whose Service-Type is not the Login-User it asked for (AcceptedServiceType, internal/component/radius/authenticator.go); the EAP form of the rule is unbuilt.

sites.quote: displayable message This is interpreted to be a human readable string of characters, and MUST NOT affect operation of the protocol.
sites.reason: Binds whichever party renders a displayable message. In ze's admin login that party is ze, which holds the operator's session. Captured as RFC3579-1.2-1 at [MUST NOT].

sites.quote: The message encoding MUST follow the UTF-8 transformation format [RFC2279].
sites.reason: Same actor as site 1.2:1: the encoding rule for the message ze would render. Captured as RFC3579-1.2-2 at [MUST].

sites.quote: On receiving a valid Access-Request packet containing EAP-Message attribute(s), a RADIUS server compliant with this specification and wishing to authenticate with EAP MUST respond with an Access-Challenge packet containing EAP-Message attribute(s).
sites.reason: Binds the RADIUS authentication server. Ze never acts as one: NewClient (internal/component/radius/client.go) binds an ephemeral UDP socket with no service port, and (*Client).readLoop dispatches a datagram only against a waiter that (*Client).Exchange registered for one of ze's own outstanding requests, so no Access-Request receive path exists in the tree. If ze ran a RADIUS server the listener would live beside that producer. The sentence names 'a RADIUS server compliant with this specification and wishing to authenticate with EAP' as the actor.

sites.quote: If the RADIUS server does not support EAP or does not wish to authenticate with EAP, it MUST respond with an Access-Reject.

If ze ran a RADIUS server the listener would live beside that producer. The actor is the RADIUS server that does not support EAP.

(*radiusAuthenticator).Authenticate returns aaa.ErrAuthRejected on CodeAccessReject today; the EAP conversation the rule ends does not exist.

sites.quote: In order to permit non-EAP aware RADIUS proxies to forward the Access-Request packet, if the NAS initially sends an EAP-Request/Identity message to the peer, the NAS MUST copy the contents of the Type-Data field of the EAP-Response/Identity received from the peer into the User-Name attribute and MUST include the Type-Data field of the EAP-Response/Identity in the User-Name attribute in every subsequent Access-Request.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS, the role ze plays: ze is the RADIUS client (internal/component/radius/client.go) and the device the operator logs in to. Captured as RFC3579-2.1-3 at [MUST].

Ze holds both secrets: the admin backend's under system/authentication/radius and the subscriber backend's under the L2TP auth-radius plugin, so it is the party that can tell reuse apart. Captured as RFC3579-4.3.4-1 at [MUST NOT].

sites.quote: Should the NAS not be able to negotiate EAP, or should the EAP-Request sent by the NAS be of a different EAP type than what is expected, the authenticating peer MUST disconnect.
sites.reason: Binds the authenticating peer. Ze fills that role: for admin login it answers EAP itself, on the operator's behalf (owner decision, 2026-09-03, plan/spec-radius-admin-eap.md), and its EAP peer is internal/core/eap. Captured as RFC3579-4.3.6-1 at [MUST].

sites.quote: An authenticating peer expecting EAP to be negotiated for a session MUST NOT negotiate a weaker method, such as CHAP or PAP.
sites.reason: Same peer role as site 4.3.6:1. The admin backend's auth-method leaf is where a fall back from EAP to CHAP or PAP would be visible. Captured as RFC3579-4.3.6-2 at [MUST NOT].

sites.quote: In such cases, if any peers of the NAS MUST do EAP, then the NAS MUST attempt to negotiate EAP for every session.
sites.reason: Binds the NAS, the role ze plays: ze is the RADIUS client (internal/component/radius/client.go) and the device the operator logs in to. Ze's PPP NAS is internal/component/l2tp/ppp, which offers PAP, CHAP-MD5 and MS-CHAPv2. Captured as RFC3579-4.3.6-3 at [MUST].

sites.quote: However, if CHAP has been negotiated but EAP is required, the RADIUS server MUST respond with an Access-Reject, rather than an Access-Challenge/EAP-Message/EAP-Request packet.
sites.reason: Binds the RADIUS authentication server. Ze never acts as one: NewClient (internal/component/radius/client.go) binds an ephemeral UDP socket with no service port, and (*Client).readLoop dispatches a datagram only against a waiter that (*Client).Exchange registered for one of ze's own outstanding requests, so no Access-Request receive path exists in the tree. If ze ran a RADIUS server the listener would live beside that producer. The actor is the RADIUS server answering a CHAP Access-Request where EAP is required.

sites.quote: The authenticating peer MUST refuse to renegotiate authentication, even if the renegotiation is from CHAP to EAP.
sites.reason: Binds the authenticating peer, the role ze fills for admin login. Captured as RFC3579-4.3.6-4 at [MUST].

sites.quote: If EAP is negotiated but is not supported by the RADIUS proxy or server, then the server or proxy MUST respond with an Access-Reject.
sites.reason: Binds the RADIUS authentication server. Ze never acts as one: NewClient (internal/component/radius/client.go) binds an ephemeral UDP socket with no service port, and (*Client).readLoop dispatches a datagram only against a waiter that (*Client).Exchange registered for one of ze's own outstanding requests, so no Access-Request receive path exists in the tree. If ze ran a RADIUS server the listener would live beside that producer. The actor is 'the server or proxy' that does not support EAP. Ze is neither a RADIUS server nor a RADIUS proxy: it forwards no other party's RADIUS packet.

sites.quote: In these cases, a PPP NAS MUST send an LCP-Terminate and disconnect the peer.
sites.reason: Binds a PPP NAS, which ze is (internal/component/l2tp/ppp, the LNS side). Captured as RFC3579-4.3.6-5 at [MUST].

sites.quote: An EAP-capable authenticating peer MUST refuse to renegotiate the authentication protocol if EAP had initially been negotiated.
sites.reason: Restates site 4.3.6:5 one paragraph later, for an EAP-capable peer rather than for the peer generally. It adds no obligation RFC3579-4.3.6-4 does not already carry.

sites.quote: A RADIUS server MUST use the source IP address of the RADIUS UDP packet to decide which shared secret to use, so that RADIUS requests can be proxied.
sites.reason: The sentence is the body of a block quotation introduced by '[RFC2865] Section 3 states:'. The obligation belongs to RFC 2865, whose summary is rfc/short/rfc2865.md, and it binds the RADIUS server in any case.
